_meta.indication: Treatment of adults with polycythemia vera.

pivotal_trials.design: Prospective, multicenter, single-arm, open-label, phase 1/2 dose-escalation trial of 7.5 years duration.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with polycythemia vera diagnosed by WHO or PVSG criteria plus JAK2 mutation positivity; newly diagnosed untreated and prior-hydroxyurea patients.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Complete hematological response (CHR) determined at 12 months, defined as HCT <45% without phlebotomy for at least 2 months, PLTs <400 x 10^9/L, WBCs <10 x 10^9/L, normal spleen and no thrombosis.
pivotal_trials.result: CHR was 31/51 (60.8%) (95% CI: 46.1%, 74.2%); median duration of response 14.3 months (95% CI: 5.5, 30.1).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>40%) were influenza-like illness, arthralgia, fatigue, pruritus, nasopharyngitis, and musculoskeletal pain. Serious adverse events occurred in 38/51 (54.9%); those in ≥4% included urinary tract infection (8%), transient ischemic attack (6%) and depression (4%).
target_moa: Interferon alfa (type I interferon) that binds the interferon alfa receptor (IFNAR), activating JAK1/TYK2 and STAT signaling; therapeutic effects in PV act on the bone marrow though not fully elucidated.
modality: Peptide/protein — a mono-PEGylated interferon alfa-2b (interferon protein).

boxed_warning.content: Risk of Serious Disorders: Interferon alfa products may cause or aggravate fatal or life-threatening neuropsychiatric, autoimmune, ischemic, and infectious disorders; monitor closely and withdraw therapy with persistently severe or worsening signs or symptoms.

rems.type: DRM and DNH determined that a REMS is not necessary to ensure the benefits of ropeginterferon alfa-2b-njft outweigh its risks.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because it did not raise significant public health questions.

orphan_indication.text: Granted orphan drug designation for the treatment of polycythemia vera by the FDA on April 2, 2012.

summary.text: BLA 761166 for BESREMi held orphan drug designation for polycythemia vera (granted April 2, 2012). After a first-cycle Complete Response letter (March 12, 2021) for human factors deficiencies, the applicant resubmitted (constituting a complete response to the March 12, 2021 action letter) and was approved; the application was not referred to an advisory committee and did not require a REMS.
